note: Printed claims only (Step 6). 50 wires, no errata (none on the errata sheet for Book IV page 85); wire list image-read at 300 dpi from PDF p.91 and identical to the OCR list. Printed procedure: enter a binary number 0-15 on slide switches 3-6, push pushbutton 6, the rotary switch indicates its decimal equivalent. Only the two endpoints are asserted: binary 15 (all four switches LEFT) and binary 0 (all four RIGHT), whose dial value does not depend on which of switches 3-6 is the high-order bit. The LEFT = 1 / RIGHT = 0 convention is not on p.85; it is the Book IV convention stated on p.80 (PDF p.86, Experiment 8: '(A slide switch RIGHT represents 0; a slide switch LEFT represents 1.)') and used without exception on p.75 (PDF p.81: 'Move slide switch 6 to the RIGHT: input A is now 0.'), p.77 (PDF p.83: 'Move slide switch 6 to the LEFT; input A is now 1.') and p.79 (PDF p.85: 'Enter the subtrahend (101) by moving slide switches 4 and 6 to the LEFT, leaving slide switch 5 RIGHT.'), so these asserts rest on that cross-page reading. All other values 1-14 need the bit order of switches 3-6, which p.85 does not print, and are left to Step 7; the nearest printed basis is Book IV p.77 (PDF p.83), 'For example, to enter binary 4 (100) set slide switch 4 LEFT, slide switch 5 RIGHT and slide switch 6 RIGHT.', which covers switches 4-6 only. Script: 15, then 0, then 15 again (so each value is reached by a dial run from the other). pb6 (6X/D17, 6Y/6+) is the motor's only feed, so it is held until the dial has stopped on the energized pad; the hold length is a script choice. Each value is an until (wiper reaches the pad), then a dwell with pb6 still held and a second expect (the dial rests there under the STOP short), then a release and a third expect. Start dial position D0 and the all-LEFT start of the slide switches (contract travel 0 = LEFT) are the construction state, not printed, so the first switch commands restate it. Rotary run rate, coast and geometry are profile fallbacks O-R1, O-R3, O-R5; maxMs and dwell windows are sized for a run rate as slow as 25 rpm. Tom ruled 2026-10-14 (DECISIONS; open-questions O-C12) that Book IV p.80's convention counts as printed for Book IV's later binary programs, this one included.
